query: Destiny Rings: Proximity-powered dating, social & networking review

results.title: Destiny Rings: Proximity-powered dating, social & networking
results.content:
There are three modes — Dating, Social, and Networking — so it's not just for romance. Whether you're trying to meet people at a happy hour, make friends in a new city, or connect with someone in your industry at a conference, the mechanic is the same: real proximity, real timing, real people.  
  
We're launching first in Hoboken, NJ before expanding to Jersey City and NYC. The app is live now (ring hardware is in final validation), so you can try Go Live mode today without a ring — proximity, Signals, and Fate Check all work through the app alone.  
  
Would love your feedback, especially on the onboarding flow and what would make this feel like a no-brainer to try at your next night out. Thanks for checking it out! 🙏 [...] Hey Product Hunt 👋  
  
I'm Jayson, founder of Destiny Rings. I built this because I was tired of the swipe-scroll-repeat cycle that dating and social apps trap you in — you match with someone, text for weeks, and half the time never actually meet.  
  
Destiny Rings flips that. You wear a Bluetooth-enabled smart ring, and when someone compatible is physically nearby — at a bar, a coffee shop, a networking event — the app lets you know in real time. Send a Signal, run a quick Fate Check, and if it's mutual, tap to reveal and start a real conversation on the spot. No more talking to someone for a month before meeting them, no more wondering if the profile photos were even recent. [...] Stella Reed

@destinyringsofficial That makes sense. The adjustable range sounds like a good way to handle different environments. I’m curious to see how it performs as more people start using it in real crowded places.

Destiny received a generally positive critical reception upon release. Aggregating review website Metacritic gave the Xbox One version 75/100 based on 11 reviews, and the PlayStation 4 version 76/100 based on 95 reviews. Bungie halted pre-release reviews stating that they felt the game should be graded only when its social aspects were operative and populated with "thousands of gamers" in order to give a proper assessment.
